_comment_advice: Non-blocking [advice] lines emitted after a mutating op. Each rule: hooks_into (ops, default all mutating), match (path glob), when (new-file|existing-file|always), contains (regex over ADDED content), resolve/resolveFromValidator (subprocess emitting a would-be target via exit 3 + stderr), message ({target}/{path}/{op} interpolate). See docs/validators.md#advice.
_comment_defaults: Default project/repo for payload ops that would otherwise require one. gl-issue-create reads 'gitlab_project' when the payload omits 'project'; gh-issue-create reads 'github_repo' when it omits 'repo'. Resolution order: explicit payload field > this config > the 'origin' git remote (host-matched). Omit this block to rely on git-remote auto-detect alone.

_example-rector-warm._install: composer global require dpt/mcp-rector-warm — then this server is on $PATH. Pair with validators/rector-mcp/ adapter for warm-process Rector validation. See validators/rector-mcp/README.md.

introduction:
supertool batches multiple file operations into one Bash call.

Invoke via Bash:
./supertool \
    'read:src/app/Module.py' \
    'read:src/app/Config.py' \
    'grep:class:src/app/:20' \
    'glob:src/app/**/*.py'

Rules:
- One call, many ops. 6-7 per call is normal. Each separate call wastes money.
- Paths are relative to project root.
- Single quotes around each op.
- Use Read tool ONLY for the file you're about to Edit — supertool for everything else.

@file payload route (mutating ops only — edit, replace, replace_lines, paste, vim):
- Inline:  ./supertool 'edit:::OLD:::NEW:::PATH'
- Payload: ./supertool 'edit:@-' <<'EOF' ... EOF   (or 'edit:@path.toml')
- Format auto-detected: starts with { or [ → JSON; else TOML.
- TOML '''triple-single-quote''' preserves backslashes/quotes/newlines byte-for-byte — use for code blocks. Single-quoted 'literal' for one-liners with \e etc.
- Content that itself contains ''' closes the block early — use a """basic""" block (escapes apply) or the JSON form, which needs no delimiter.
- Field names match the syntax tokens lowercased (edit:::OLD:::NEW:::PATH → old, new, path).

To avoid escape problems, use chr(10)/chr(27) instead of \n/\x1b in payload content.
output-format:
Each operation returns a header followed by its output:

```
--- read:src/app/Module.py ---
(45 lines, 1230 bytes)
     1→import os
     2→import sys
     3→
     4→class Module:

--- grep:class:src/app/:5 ---
(2 results, limit 5)
src/app/Module.py
  4:class Module:
src/app/Config.py
  8:class Config:

--- glob:src/app/**/*.py ---
(3 files)
src/app/Module.py
src/app/Config.py
src/app/Utils.py
```

read.description: Read file (300 lines, 20KB cap). Set abstract:1 to return a tree-sitter symbol map instead of raw source for any file over abstract_threshold_bytes (php, python, js/jsx, ts/tsx, go, rust, java, ruby, c, cpp, swift, kotlin, scala, lua, bash), median 5% of the source bytes; falls back to raw source and names the reason when the map would be empty or no smaller. php_abstract is the former name and still enables it — saves tokens on big files. Use :full to force raw. Threshold override: SUPERTOOL_READ_ABSTRACT_THRESHOLD_BYTES=N Inline grep= filter contains ':'? Use read:@payload.toml or read:@- (fields: path, offset, limit, grep, full).

read-grep.description: Inline filter — matching lines, line nums kept

grep.description: Search (10 results def). CONTEXT=N lines around match. Lines capped at max_line_chars (500). :no-auto-read suppresses single-file auto-read Pattern contains ':'? The colon CLI can't tell where it ends — use grep:@payload.toml or grep:@- (fields: pattern, path, limit, context, count, no_auto_read).

grep-count.description: Count mode — match counts/file, no content

around.description: First match + N lines ctx (def 10). 1-shot grep+read. Output capped ~16KB (max_bytes) — truncates at line boundary Pattern contains ':'? Use around:@payload.toml or around:@- (fields: pattern, path, n).

grep_around.description: Every match + N ctx lines (def 3, limit 10). Bulk usage scan. Output capped ~16KB (max_bytes) — truncates at line boundary Pattern contains ':'? Use grep_around:@payload.toml or grep_around:@- (fields: pattern, path, n, limit).

glob.description: Find files (**). Unanchored no-match retried as **/PATTERN. Auto-reads concrete paths

around_line.description: N lines around LINE (def 10). Target marked →

between.description: Chunk of file. Symbol mode (tree-sitter, multi-lang; source-shaped names OK: 'async function foo') or re:START:END pattern mode SYMBOL/START/END contains ':'? Use between:@payload.toml or between:@- (fields: symbol | start+end, path).

blame.description: Git blame N lines around LINE (def 5)

replace_dry.description: Preview a replace without writing — shows -old/+new per match. Use ::: when content has ':'.

replace.description: Replace every OLD→NEW across PATH (file or dir), returns a receipt. Auto-validates per file type, rolls back on syntax fail. Use ::: when content has ':'.

edit.description: Single-file edit, OLD must match exactly once. Bypasses native Edit must-Read state — saves a round-trip. Use ::: separator so content with ':' works.

replace_lines.description: Swap lines [START,END] (1-indexed inclusive) with CONTENT. END<START = insert before START. Empty CONTENT = delete.

append.description: Append CONTENT to end of file. Creates it if missing. Adds a missing trailing newline first. Use instead of wc + replace_lines with an inverted range.

paste.description: Replace entire file with CONTENT. Atomic, creates file (+ parent dirs) if missing. Use for full-file rewrites.

vim.description: Cursor-based multi-action edit parsed like a vim macro — the DEFAULT op for pattern-based edits (find+change, insert relative to a pattern, multi-step chains). NORMAL verbs read char-by-char; insert/search/ex verbs enter greedy modes until \e (ESC, U+001B). Fall back to paste (full file) / edit (unique literal swap) / replace_lines (known range) when vim doesn't fit. Full reference: ./supertool help vim.

validate.description: Run registered validators matching PATH (by extension). Pass a comma-separated PATH list to validate many files in one call (config loaded once for the batch; each path security-checked at dispatch). Optional tool_filter limits to named validators; the special filter `@syntax` selects only parser/compiler validators (those with `"syntax": true`). Same validators that fire after every mutating op. Append `verbose` for uncapped errors + source context + raw stdout/stderr.

gc.description: Prune supertool's own caches (~/.cache/supertool). Bare `gc` and `gc:dry` PREVIEW — per-kind counts and bytes, nothing deleted. `gc:run` deletes. Optional KIND scopes to one of vim-cursor, vim-undo, vi-cursor, validators. Retention per kind (7d vim, 30d validators) via the `gc` block in .supertool.json. Entries whose age can't be determined are never removed. Runs automatically at most once an hour.

format.description: Run registered formatters matching PATH (writes file in place). Optional tool_filter limits to named formatters. Same formatters that fire after every mutating op. Append `verbose` for uncapped errors + source context + raw stdout/stderr.

validate_staged.description: Run validators on all files in git diff --cached --name-only. Optional tool_filter. Pre-commit check across the full staged diff. Append `verbose` for full per-file details.

format_staged.description: Run formatters on all staged files. Pair with validate_staged for a normalize-then-check pass. Append `verbose` for full per-file details.

batch.description: Run an array of ops in one call. Mix anything — read+edit+grep+phpstan in one round-trip. Payload: bare array of {op, ...fields} OR wrapper {continue_on_error, ops}. Default continue. Validators fire per mutating op. JSON only (TOML can't express bare arrays). Use @- for stdin.

workspace.description: One-shot IDE-style view: file + symbols + validators + siblings + git + references + tests. Opt-in (heavy). Use for first-touch on unfamiliar files.

resolve.description: Symbol → file. LSP via mcp.tools.resolve when configured, else heuristic glob.

hover.description: LSP hover: type + docs for SYMBOL.

rename.description: LSP workspace rename. Safer than sed.

_comment_exclude_paths: Paths are RELATIVE to cwd. Two match modes: (1) single segment like 'vendor/' matches that name anywhere in the tree; (2) multi-segment like 'src/legacy/generated/' anchors at repo root. Built-in defaults (.git/, node_modules/, __pycache__/, .venv/, venv/, dist/, build/, .idea/, .vscode/, .svn/, .hg/) are merged additively — list only project-specific extras.

mypy.description: Type-check a Python file with mypy.

pytest.description: Run pytest on a test file or directory.

ruff.description: Lint a Python file with ruff.

job.description: Inspect a CI job by ID. Extra keys below pass through to the script as SUPERTOOL_* env vars — tune behavior from JSON without editing scripts.

gl-mrs.description: MR triage board. Override the gitlab preset's defaults to tune pipeline enrichment — extra keys pass through as SUPERTOOL_ENRICH_WORKERS / SUPERTOOL_ENRICH_CAP / SUPERTOOL_PER_PAGE.

dashboard._doc: The lane board's label vocabulary. There is NO default: with lane_prefix absent, dashboard prints the lanes section as `!! unread` and names this key, because a prefix nobody chose selects zero labels and renders byte-identically to a repository with no work in flight (#1007, the same property as radar_tiers/#528). Spell it exactly as your labels do — claude-supertool uses `lane-` (lane-watch, lane-release), while claude-remember spells the sibling namespace `priority:high` with a colon. When a configured prefix matches nothing, the section says so and names the labels that share its stem behind another separator; it never silently tries the other one. Passes through as SUPERTOOL_DASHBOARD_LANE_PREFIX.

radar._doc: Radar reconciles registered tiers against live truth. There is NO default tier: with radar_tiers absent or empty, radar refuses and names the fix, because an unconfigured radar that prints nothing is byte-identical to a healthy one. 'gl-mrs' is the GitLab MR board (the whole of radar before #528); 'gl-runners' adds the runner fleet and needs Maintainer to read project runners. Registration order is render order. Both keys pass through as SUPERTOOL_RADAR_TIERS / SUPERTOOL_RADAR_EXCLUSIONS.

19509.reason: MySQL service TLS failure + standing conflict, not this MR

git-commit._doc: Overrides the git preset's git-commit op. 'coauthor' passes through as SUPERTOOL_COAUTHOR — the Co-Authored-By trailer auto-appended when the commit message lacks one (default 'Max <noreply>'). Set to '' / 'none' / 'off' / 'false' to disable.

_hidden_internal.description: Hidden from `./supertool ops` output via status:0 — useful for ops that exist for aliases or scripts but shouldn't clutter the public listing.

qa.description: Full quality check: lint, types, tests.

context.description: Bootstrap context for a file: contents + sibling symbols + TODOs.

_example-opt-in-strict._doc: opt_in=true gates the validator behind explicit `validate:PATH:_example-opt-in-strict` calls — never runs after edits. Use for expensive or noisy checks you only want on demand.

_example-resolve-to-test._doc: After editing src/foo.py, `resolve` rewrites the target to tests/test_foo.py before running pytest on it. Shell cmd that prints an alternate path on stdout.
